text:
NEW YORK, NY / ACCESSWIRE / May 24, 2018 / Apple shares were little changed on Wednesday despite the New York Times reporting that the iPhone maker has teamed up with Volkswagen to make self-driving cars for Apple employees. Shares of Hewlett Packard saw a big loss after reporting first quarter results and lackluster guidance for the second quarter.
RDI Initiates Coverage on:
Hewlett Packard Enterprise Company
https://rdinvesting.com/news/?ticker=HPE
Apple Inc.
https://rdinvesting.com/news/?ticker=AAPL
Hewlett Packard Enterprise Company shares closed down 10.51% on about 56 million shares traded. The big drop came after the computer tech company announced second quarter financial results wherein the CEO warned of a "challenging second half." For the quarter, net revenue saw a growth of 9.7% YOY and hit $7.47 billion. Adjusted net income was $536 million, or 34 cents per diluted share. This was ahead of the earnings of 31 cents per share analysts had expected. Revenue was also ahead of the $7.38 billion expected by analysts. CEO Antonio Neri stated, "I'm very pleased with our strong performance in Q2. We continue to execute well across all business segments while delivering on a number of strategic initiatives." Looking ahead however, the company projects that third quarter adjusted earnings will be in the range of 35 cents to 39 cents. Analysts were waiting for 36 cents.

Apple Inc. shares closed up a modest 0.64% on Wednesday with lackluster volume of nearly 16 million shares traded compared to the average volume of 32 million shares. The tech giant has inked a deal with Volkswagen to make self driving cars for its employees according to a New York Times report. The agreement is for Volkswagen's new, boxy T6 Transporter vans. The two companies have teamed up to modify the vans into self-driving shuttles for Apple workers. The project is the primary focus of the iPhone maker's autonomous driving unit and is behind schedule according to the report. In other news Apple is also offering a partial refund to some customers who paid full price for iPhone battery replacements last year. Apple said yesterday it would give a $50 credit to customers who replaced the battery in an iPhone 6 or older model between Jan. 1 and Dec. 28, 2017. The refund will reduce the cost of the battery replacement from $79 to $29, which is the price Apple started offering in late December.
